_README: The curated highlight list (features/CORRIDOR_VIEW.md, #595): stretches of
trail somebody says are worth going to, with what that claim rests on.
THIS FILE IS EDITORIAL AND SAYS SO. Every entry here carries basis
'named', which in the app reads as 'we put this on a list of well-known
routes - an editorial call, not a measurement'. It is deliberately the
weakest of the three bases. An entry ATC themselves publish as a day hike
is basis 'published' and cites ATC instead; the two coexist on one record
and the app cites the stronger.
WHY THE MILES ARE NOT IN HERE. A leg names two POIs and no numbers.
export_highlights.py resolves them against the PUBLISHED POI records to
get the miles, exactly as export_spurs.py resolves a spur's destination
and for the same reason: the ids have to be the ones already on the
device. It also means the mile range is ATC's own measurement rather than
somebody typing a figure out of a guidebook into this file.
WHY BOTH ENDS ARE THINGS ATC NAMED. Every anchor below is a feature ATC's
own layers carry a name for - a summit, and the trailhead parking that
serves it. That does not make the SELECTION anybody's but ours; it makes
the two ends checkable, and it keeps this file from inventing places. The
`anchors` block repeats those names in words so a reviewer reading a diff
can see what an id refers to without resolving it.
WHAT IS STILL MISSING. features/CORRIDOR_VIEW.md's target is about thirty
entries, one per maintaining club, because that is the unit that maps to
volunteering. There are ten here. The clubs with none are not an oversight
to be filled quietly - export_highlights.py prints them on every run, and
adding one is a row somebody has to stand behind.
Reviewed row by row. That is the whole reason this is committed rather
than generated - see .github/tests/test_no_committed_data.py.

highlights.name: McAfee Knob
highlights.note: The most photographed spot on the A.T.; the ledge appears on ATC's own materials and on the cover of most guides.

highlights.name: Wayah Bald
highlights.note: A stone observation tower on a bald reachable from the road, long a standard first-week landmark in North Carolina.

highlights.name: The Priest
highlights.note: Roughly 3,000 ft of climb over four miles; known among thru-hikers by name rather than by mile.

highlights.name: Stony Man
highlights.note: The short cliff-top walk in Shenandoah that most day visitors to the park are pointed at.

highlights.name: Killington Peak
highlights.note: Vermont's second-highest summit, a named side trip off the A.T. that predates the trail itself.

highlights.name: Mahoosuc Arm
highlights.note: The climb out of Mahoosuc Notch, routinely named alongside the Notch as the hardest ground in Maine.

highlights.name: Baldpate East Peak
highlights.note: Open ledge above Grafton Notch, one of the standard day hikes from that trailhead.

highlights.name: Saddleback Mountain
highlights.note: Miles of open ridge above treeline, among the most exposed walking in Maine.

highlights.name: Old Blue Mountain
highlights.note: A short steep climb to an open summit, the usual day objective from South Arm Road.

highlights.name: Moxie Bald

anchors.from: Troutdale Rd Jo's Hole Parking Area

highlights.note: Bare granite summit in the Hundred-Mile Wilderness approach, named on ATC's own layer.
